translations.text: And what is this saying that he spoke: “Let whoever has ears listen”?
And be innocent like doves. Guard yourselves against people who have the nature of beasts rather than human beings.
For the race of those beasts will not disappear until the end of the age.
And neither will the race of the blessed sheep of the flock of the good shepherd, Christ, disappear until the end of the age.
Especially that sort of people who live in idleness, according to what is written: “Every idle person is full of desires.”
If Scripture said, “Be still and know that I am God,” it does not permit each person to refrain from working for their livelihood, food, and clothing.
Rather, it says, “Cease from the works of the flesh,” which are sexual immorality, idol worship, sorcery, hostilities, quarrels, jealousy, contentiousness, divisions, factions, and slanders.
Nor will they know that God is God, as Scripture said.
“For you are the one whom I have seen to be righteous before me in this generation.”
Then again, Jacob, whom God blessed because of his father Abraham and Isaac—does he not himself say:
“For his appearance is not the appearance of a human being.”
To the innkeeper, saying to him, “Take care of him.”
“And whatever you spend on him, I will give you when I return.” Who among these three
Then the one who will also fulfill it within his heart

When the king comes in his glory to judge between these and the others, between those on the right because of love, mercy, and the fullness of kindness toward others, and those on the left because of jealousy, hatred, and mercilessness.

“For if you love those who love you,” he said, “what reward do you have? Do not the tax collectors themselves do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing? The other nations

And the devil trembles before her at all times, filled with shame in her presence, seeing the likeness of Christ upon her and the sign of his holy cross. For it was because of his love for humanity and his mercy toward human beings that he endured the cross.
So that we may know that all the words of Scripture oppose this practice from the beginning.
For our holy father Apa Athanasius says, “Preserve the honorable human likeness, for they will not call you a human being,” he said, “if you do the deeds of irrational creatures.”
If we have done a little, they will proclaim much more, and they tell one another about many good deeds, saying, “We do them.”

Even if the heart of the ungodly person is filled with defilement from it, he cannot carry out his impurities with his mouth unless he finds someone like himself, under this same curse, burning to hear of his neighbor’s wickedness and disgrace.
So that he may take still greater pleasure in insulting many people who are better than he is, just like the prostitute who displays herself in the streets, serving as a snare.
Still more, so that they may delight in a delight full of weeping without knowing it, and rejoice with a false joy over the humiliation of their neighbors, a joy full of grief, without realizing it.
Then, when it grows, it becomes larger than the vegetables and becomes a large tree, so that the birds of the sky come and dwell beneath its branches.
Blessed are you, Lord God Almighty.
John. Exposition.
For the anger of a king is like the roaring of a lion, as he teaches godlessness and the destruction of the souls of multitudes,
having such a great threat at his disposal,
and an anger that cannot be appeased with money.
Then how much more the King of heaven and earth, the Creator of everything,
who created everything out of what did not exist—the heavens and the earth,
the sea and everything in it—will he not be angry?
Woe to everyone who neglects to leave sin behind until he dies,
as we have said many times.
We ought to become wise, like all those who became wise through the abundance of the words of Scripture, as it has called us to repentance from the beginning.

Or does Scripture not say, “A whip for a horse, and a bridle for a donkey, but a rod for a foolish nation”? What is the rod for the foolish nation if not the words of Scripture, according to what is written?

We are the ones who commit acts of lawlessness, although we cannot bear the anger of God’s wrath. We provoke him constantly through our evil deeds, especially we who live in the places of Christ—the priests and the monks.
For even the commander of the Lord’s army, when he appeared to Joshua near Jericho, did not refrain from saying it to him.

Just as the ancient giants and all the people who perished were not spared to see Noah and his entire household, who were saved, so sinful people or lawless brothers will not be spared to see righteous brothers in their rest and their joy, when they themselves die in their evil deeds.
As he spoke with them through the holy prophet Moses and Aaron,
he has spared no one who sins in any way, from the beginning of creation until now, from being cast down into Hades.
